APPROVAL OF MINUTES
  EL MONTE CITY COUNCIL ADJOURNED REGULAR MEETING
  OF JUNE 23, 2020

MEETING JOINTLY AND REGULARLY WITH THE EL MONTE HOUSING AUTHORITY; EL
MONTE PUBLIC FINANCING AUTHORITY; EL MONTE WATER AUTHORITY; EL MONTE
PARKING AUTHORITY; SUCCESSOR AGENCY TO THE FORMER EL MONTE COMMUNITY
REDEVELOPMENT AGENCY; HOUSING SUCCESSOR AGENCY; AND, FROM TIME TO
TIME, SUCH OTHER BODIES OF THE CITY WHOSE MEMBERSHIP IS COMPOSED
EXCLUSIVELY OF THE MEMBERSHIP OF THE CITY COUNCIL

1.  CALL TO ORDER: 6:05 p.m.

2.  ROLL CALL FOR CITY COUNCIL AND AUTHORITY BODIES:

  Andre Quintero, Mayor/Chair – present
  Maria Morales, Mayor Pro Tem/Authority Member – present
  Jessica Ancona, Councilmember/Authority Member – present
  Victoria Martinez Muela, Councilmember/Authority Member – present
  Jerry Velasco, Councilmember/Authority Member – present

3.  APPROVAL OF AGENDA:

  WITH THE FOLLOWING EDITS/CHANGES TO THE AGENDA:

  SPECIALLY ADDED AGENDA ITEM:

  s) Mayor Pro Tem Morales  5-0

4.  CLOSED SESSION (6:00 p.m. – 7:00 p.m.): None

  The City Council and the various Authority Bodies whose membership is composed
  exclusively of the membership of the City Council (collectively, the “Council”) will attempt
  to address and complete all Closed Session business between 6:00 p.m. and 7:00 p.m.
  If the Council completes all Closed Session business prior to 7:00 p.m., the Council will
  take a short recess and commence all Open Session proceedings promptly at 7:00 p.m.
  In the event the City Council is unable to address or complete all agendized Closed
  Session items by 7:00 p.m., the Council will hear all such remaining items toward the
  end of the meeting, immediately following Council Communications. Should any member
  of the public wish to address the Council on any agendized Closed Session matter, the
  Council shall allow such person to address the Council on such matter prior to going into
  Closed Session, provided that all persons wishing to address the Council on an
  agendized Closed Session matter shall fill out a speaker card and be subject to a
   City Council Adjourned Meeting Minutes of June 23, 2020

speaker’s time limit of 3 minutes per speaker and further provided that the Council shall
be under no obligation to respond to or deliberate upon any specific questions or
comments posed by a speaker or take action on any issue raised by a speaker beyond
such action as the City Council may be lawfully authorized to take on an agendized
Closed Session matter pursuant to the Brown Act (Govt. Code Section 54950 et seq.).

Mayor Quintero invited members of the public to address the City Council on
Closed Session Items 4.1 through 4.4.

Mayor Quintero and the City Council recessed into Closed Session at
approximately 6:06 p.m. Mayor Quintero and the City Council reconvened from
Closed Session at approximately 7:21 pm.

respect to Items 4.1 through 4.4.

7.  PUBLIC COMMENT REGARDING NON-AGENDIZED MATTERS: None

  This time has been set aside for persons in the audience to make comments or inquiries
  on matters within the general subject matter jurisdiction of the City Council, the Housing
  Authority, the Financing Authority and/or the Water Authority (collectively, the “Council”)
  that are not listed on this agenda. Although no person is required to provide their
  name and address as a condition to attending a Council meeting, persons who wish to
  address the Council are asked to state their name and address. Each speaker will be
  limited to three (3) continuous minutes. Speakers may not lend any portion of their
  speaking time to other persons or borrow additional time from other persons.

  Except as otherwise provided under the Brown Act (Gov. Code Section 54950 et seq.),
  the Council may not deliberate or take action upon any matter not listed on this posted
  agenda but may order that any such matter be placed on the agenda for a subsequent
  meeting. The Council may also direct staff to investigate certain matters for
  consideration at a future meeting.

  3
   City Council Adjourned Meeting Minutes of June 23, 2020

  All comments or queries presented by a speaker shall be addressed to the Council as a
  body and not to any specific member thereof. No questions shall be posed to any
  member of the Council except through the presiding official of the meeting, the Mayor
  and/or Chair. Members of the Council are under no obligation to respond to questions
  posed by speakers but may provide brief clarifying responses to any comment made or
  questions posed. The Council may not engage in any sort of prolonged discussion or
  deliberation with any speaker or group of speakers on matters that are not listed on this
  agenda.

  Enforcement of Decorum: The Chief of Police, or such member, or members of the
  Police Department as the Chief of Police may designate, shall serve as the Sergeant-at-
  Arms of any Council meeting. The Sergeant-at-Arms shall carry out all orders and
  instructions given by the presiding official for the purpose of maintaining order and
  decorum at the meeting. While members of the public are free to level criticism of City
  policies and the action(s) or proposed action(s) of the Council or its members, members
  of the public may not engage in behavior that is disruptive to the orderly conduct of the
  proceedings, including, but not limited to, conduct that prevents other members of the
  public from being heard when it is their opportunity to speak or which prevents members
  of the audience from hearing or seeing the proceedings. Members of the public may not
  threaten any person with physical harm or act in a manner that may reasonably be
  interpreted as an imminent threat of physical harm. All persons attending the meeting
  must adhere to the City’s policy barring harassment based upon a person’s race,
  religious creed, color, national origin, ancestry, physical handicap, medical condition,
  marital status, gender, sexual orientation or age.

8.2  Second Reading of an Ordinance of the City Council of the City of El Monte,
  California Amending Chapter 8.10 (Retail Sales of Tobacco Products) of Title 8
  (Health and Safety) of the El Monte Municipal Code to Prohibit the Sale of
  Flavored Tobacco Products, Effective as of January 1, 2021.
  RECOMMENDATION OF BUSINESS ITEM UNDER CONSIDERATION:

  It is recommended that the City Council:

  1. Ratify the proposed Ordinance for second reading by no less than three
  votes.

  Total Cost: N/A  Account No:  N/A
  Is the cost of this item budgeted? N/A

  Ordinance No. 2980

  Annie Tegen - The Campaign for Tobacco-Free Kids would like to thank El
  Monte City Council for their strong leadership last week on this life-saving
  ordinance. I’d like to thank you for standing up for kids, and fighting back against
  the decades of targeting by the tobacco industry. We strongly support the
  ordinance to end the sale of flavored tobacco products in all retailers, including
  menthol cigarettes and all flavored cigars. This is a critical step that will help
  protect children living in El Monte from the unrelenting efforts by the tobacco
  industry to hook them to a deadly addiction. The flavors lure kids in, and the
  nicotine hooks them. Flavored tobacco products are designed to alter the taste
  and reduce the harshness of tobacco products so they are more appealing and
  easy for beginners, who are almost always kids. These products are pervasive
  and are marketed and sold in a variety of kid-friendly flavors. With their colorful
  packaging and sweet flavors, flavored tobacco products are often hard to
  distinguish from the candy displays near which they are frequently placed in retail
  outlets and often at eye level for kids. Menthol is the most popular tobacco flavor
  among youth. Most insidious among the flavors preferred by youth, are mint and
  menthol. Tobacco companies have a long history of targeting and marketing

  5
   City Council Adjourned Meeting Minutes of June 23, 2020

flavored tobacco products to African Americas and youth. As a result of this
targeting, 85 percent of African American smokers smoke menthol cigarettes,
compared to 29 percent of white smokers. Use of menthol cigarettes leads to a
disproportionate health burden for African Americans. The tobacco industry’s
“investment” in the African American community has had a destructive impact.
The scientific evidence leaves no doubt that menthol cigarettes and other
flavored tobacco products increase the number of people, particularly kids, who
try the product, become addicted and die a premature death as a result. Ending
the all flavored tobacco products is an important step toward protecting our
children from the tobacco industry’s aggressive efforts to hook children to a
deadly, addictive product.

Tony Kuo - The County of Los Angeles is committed to protecting the health and
well-being of youth and the general public. Both the FDA and the U.S. Surgeon
General have warned that flavored tobacco products, such as electronic smoking
devices and little cigars and cigarillos, help new users establish habits that can
lead to long-term addiction. Flavored e-cigarettes are not tested nor are
approved smoking cessation devices and may expose users to high levels of
nicotine. Prohibiting the sale of flavored tobacco products will help prevent
tobacco-related disease and death. Menthol cigarettes have been shown to
increase youth initiation, inhibit cessation, and promote relapse. Scientific studies
have shown that because of its sensory effects and flavor (minty taste and
cooling sensation) menthol may enhance the addictiveness of cigarettes.
Although the use of cigarettes is declining in the U.S., sales of menthol cigarettes
have steadily increased in recent years, especially among young people and new
smokers. For these reasons, on September 24, 2019, the County of Los Angeles
Board of Supervisors approved an ordinance creating restrictions on retail sales
of tobacco products. The new restrictions and requirements apply to tobacco
retailers in the unincorporated area of the County. The law does not apply to
personal possession or use of tobacco products. Beginning May 1, 2020,
retailers are no longer able to sell any flavored tobacco or flavored tobacco
products, including, but not limited to, menthol cigarettes, hookah tobacco, and
flavored products meant for use in electronic smoking devices. Tobacco flavored
tobacco products may continue to be sold.

Arabi Hassan - BREATHE CA of Los Angeles County strong urges you to pass a
full flavor ban in the City of El Monte, including all flavored tobacco products such
as menthol, spearmint, and mint products. Any exemptions will weaken the
ordinance and create loopholes for young people to access flavored tobacco
products that lure them into using addictive, nicotine products. Please make the
health of your constituents a priority. Over 80% of youth who start using tobacco
for the first time, start with a flavored product like menthol cigarettes. These
products are designed to mark the harsh taste of tobacco and lure children as
young as 10 into using products that taste like cotton candy, bubble gum,
strawberry, among many others. These products, which contain nicotine, cause
long-term damage to adolescent brain and have been driving tobacco-related
deaths and diseases across the country. Your actions will prevent a new
generation of young smokers from becoming addicted to these addictive
products.

  6
   City Council Adjourned Meeting Minutes of June 23, 2020

Yaneth Rodriguez – I would like to commend you for your leadership in
considering a comprehensive policy that will restrict the sale of flavored tobacco
products, including menthol cigarettes and hookah, with no exemptions. As you
consider the health of the community, in particular during this unprecedented
time with COVID-19, you are also thinking of the health of future generations.
Attached is an information sheet which contains research findings from the
University of Southern California's Tobacco Center of Regulatory Science (USC
TCORS). I hope this information is useful in your consideration of this policy. A
main research point I would like to highlight is that an ordinance to regulate e-
cigarettes, flavored, and menthol tobacco products has tremendous potential to
substantially reduce youth-use of tobacco products including e-cigarettes. A
Southern California research study showed that strong enforcement preventing
sales to minors was associated with lower rates of youth and adult initiation of
combustible and e-cigarette use. Current research suggests that it is important to
consider the overall impact of e-cigarette and tobacco use on all segments of the
population; however, the weight of the evidence points to a far more detrimental
effect on youth.

Christy Zamani – I would like to thank you for your leadership in supporting a ban
on flavored tobacco products in the City of El Monte. In passing this important
and effective safeguard you will be joining a number of neighboring cities in
protecting youth from a lifetime of tobacco use and addiction. Hopefully, after
passing this public health victory you can explore further restrictions on
smoking/vaping in outdoor public spaces. As a mother of a three year old, who
likes to frequently dine outdoors I believe all people should have a right to safe,
smokefree areas. Thank you for protecting the health of the El Monte
Community.

Primo Castro – Thank you, Mayor Quintero and Council members, for discussing
this important issue. We encourage the council to support this ordinance that
ends the sale of all flavored tobacco products, including menthol flavored
cigarettes in the city. Tobacco companies have a long history of marketing to
vulnerable populations, and target youth with imagery and by marketing
appealing flavors. Actions taken now at the local level can help to encourage a
generation of tobacco-free kids—potentially saving them from a lifetime of
addiction and the deadly consequences of tobacco use. We ask the City of El
Monte to join local neighbors in the name of Public Health enacting policies
without any menthol exemption. Our communities of color and low-income
communities have been targeted for far too long and eliminating the sale of
flavored tobacco products, including menthol cigarettes, is the way to address
the targeting of our youth. These are the same communities who already bear a
greater burden of health disparities, such as cancer, heart disease and many
other chronic diseases associated with tobacco use.

Amanda Staples – The American Heart Association is in proud support of Item
#8.2 – ending the sale of flavored tobacco. There is no price for health - And
ending the sale of all flavored tobacco will reduce access to the products that
target and addict new smokers, particularly youth. We are so grateful to our
STEM Go Red youth that came to speak in support of this effort in early March.
This is a leading concern for our cohort of young women and will welcome the
news of this important measure. Thank you for championing health in El Monte.

  7
   City Council Adjourned Meeting Minutes of June 23, 2020

  We ask the City Council to continue to make the health of El Monte youth and all
  its residents a priority and join our neighbors in the many communities
  throughout California who have adopted strong policies to end the sale of
  flavored tobacco products. We urge you to end the sale of all flavored tobacco
  products citywide, including menthol cigarettes, flavored e-cigarettes, and all
  other flavored tobacco products.

  Tomas Torices – The American Academy of Pediatrics California Chapter we are
  in full support of a ban on the sale of all flavored tobacco products, including
  electronic flavored devices, in the City of El Monte. We are in the midst of an
  increasing teenage vaping epidemic. Reducing access to flavored tobacco
  products is crucial. MENTHOL: The tobacco industry has purposely lobbied to
  keep this flavor in the market. Menthol makes it easier to start smoking and
  harder to quit. The evidence is clear - decades of predatory marketing practices
  have led to over 50% of Latino smokers using menthol flavored tobacco. We also
  know that the CDC reports that 67% of Latinos want to quit, but fail due to the
  addictive effects of nicotine. Of young people (12-17 years old) who smoke, 57%
  smoke menthols. Pediatricians in Los Angeles now have to refer nicotine-
  addicted children to substance abuse specialists. VAPING: In December 2018,
  the US Surgeon General of the United States declared youth e-cigarette use an
  “epidemic. As high as 40% of middle and high school students currently use a
  liquid flavored tobacco in conjunction with an electronic device. With this in mind,
  on behalf of the local Chapter of the American Academy of Pediatrics and the El
  Monte Families Fighting Flavored Tobacco coalition, we respectfully urge you to
  protect the health of El Monte youth and families and approve a comprehensive
  ordinance that ends the sale of all flavored tobacco products, including electronic
  flavored devices, with no exemptions. We thank you for your leadership.

m) Mayor Quintero
s) Mayor Pro Tem Morales  5-0
